0116 v2 AND 0138 ARE READY FOR YOUR REVIEW. Paths are under my scratchpad, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Devbin/03c88122-8547-4528-bbc1-b59e05154dfd/scratchpad.

0116 v2: series0116v2/0001-0116-fleet-s-census-frame-is-a-tracked-file-bin-.dev.patch, sha256 d27c432c36e9055e, one commit (d6009b3 in build0116b) on the shared tree's 341ded1, the same four files as v1. WHAT CHANGED SINCE YOUR REVIEW is 0116-rework.interdiff (v1 to v2, 3 files, +121 -9):
- Should-fix 1: the variable's branch counts its roots, and a DEVBIN_FLEET_ROOTS naming none dies "fleet: DEVBIN_FLEET_ROOTS names no root", as the file does.
- Should-fix 2: .claude and the census list stay pruned by name; the home's own Library and .Trash are pruned by path, so a project's Library/ is walked. outside_unwalked holds the one sentence of what is not walked -- ~/Library (which holds CloudStorage), ~/.Trash, and anything through a symlink -- and audit's stderr, doc (its Outside section and a cannot-tell-you bullet) and upgrade's summary each print it. fleet.md says the same.
- Your (3): an arm drives upgrade over an incomplete walk, asserting the NOT KNOWN row and rc 0, after a control run with no hole. The comment at the block says why upgrade keeps its exit code.
- The message is rewritten to match, including the live measurement below and your 17 s and 52 s.
EVIDENCE. The three new arms: two are red on the handler you reviewed (the empty variable; the prune and the unwalked sentence). The third, NOT KNOWN, is green there by construction, since it holds existing behaviour, and G8 kills it. 22 mutants, each applying, each parsing under bash -n, and each killed by the arm aimed at it: G1 (the empty frame taken) by 10; G2-G7 (Library by name again, the home's Library walked, the home's .Trash walked, and each report's unwalked line dropped) by 11; G8 (NOT KNOWN dropped, your Q3) and G9 (upgrade failing over the hole) by 12; and the original set (F1-F5, F6b, F7, F8a, F8b, F9-F12) re-run against v2, each still killed by its own arm (mut0116b.results). fleet, documentation, help, doctor and localinstall on v2: 1..264, 264 ok, rc 0, 13:55:34Z to 14:02:23Z (files0116b.tap). shellcheck and the headless critic are clean on the handler. Live here at 13:50Z: audit rc 0 in 38 s with a full suite running beside it, 33 installs inside the frame, 6 outside (the machine install and five scratch worktrees), and the unwalked line printed.
THE FULL SUITE on v1's tree (build0116 at e5499bd: the series plus 0116 v1): 1..1662, 1662 ok, 0 not ok, 4 skips, 1662 distinct, rc 0, 13:18:54Z to 13:53:58Z (full0116.tap). v2 changes only the fleet files, and their affected files are the 264 above.

0138: series0138/0001-0138-builtins.bats-s-builtin-arm-reads-the-catalogue.patch, sha256 0c7cd681506740ca, one file (tests/unit/builtins.bats, +16 -2), on 341ded1. The arm reads six fields and counts what it checked, and that count is compared with a second count: every row whose command line is the literal @builtin. RED FIRST, driven: with a command row and an option row planted, each @builtin with nothing behind it, the old arm is green and the new one names both. The old five-field read under the new count fails "checked 0 @builtin rows, and the catalogue holds 27". Old read, no count, both plants: green, which is the defect as it stood. On today's catalogue the fixed arm is green, 27 of 27, so nothing was hiding behind it. builtins.bats: 1..39, 39 ok. The critic is clean on the file.

ON YOUR APPROVAL I land 0116 and then 0138, each by git commit --only with the gate running, verified path by path. Neither touches your 0120 or 0123 files, so the order among them is free. Your 0120 and 0123 reviews are next on my side.
